title: Guardana Saved Run v17
description: One Guardana run written to disk: the manifest (what was verified, against what, under which configuration and limits, at what cost, with what reach, and with what verdict) plus the finding channels. Versioned independently of the CLI.

unverified.description: Checks that ran and could not reach a verdict. Never folded into findings and never dropped: a check that could not grade is not a pass.

waived.description: Findings a baseline accepted with a reason. Still reported, no longer gating.

errors.description: Checks that could not run at all.

observations.description: What the run saw, as opposed to what it found wrong.

assessments.description: Every case this run measured, pass included. See guardana.core.assessment.

scope.description: Every file a file run listed and the excludes it applied while listing them; null for any other run, and for a run migrated from schema 11. A comparison calls a finding resolved only where the later run still listed its file.

manifest.description: The circumstances of the run. Carries no version of its own: the document above states it once.

allOf.$comment: Nullability above exists for migrated documents only. A run written at this version must record when it ran, under what limits, and how it was gated — otherwise the allowance made for migration becomes a way for a fresh run to skip them.

migrated_from.description: Which older schema this document was migrated from. Null means it was written at this version — which is how a reader tells 'this run spent nothing' from 'this run predates the version that counted'.

fingerprint_inputs.description: The fields the fingerprint was computed from. Present so no reader mistakes a digest of declared identity for a digest of model weights.

document.description: The SHA-256 of the document the run read, over its first `bytes` bytes, and what that covers: `content` is every byte of the document, `content_prefix` the bytes read before a read ceiling stopped the reader. Null means no digest was recorded (the run read no document, or was written before version 11) — never that the document matched anything.

deployment.description: Which deployment this verifies. Null means not known, never not applicable.

configuration.description: What settings produced this result, by digest rather than by content.

provider.description: The provider wire the run spoke to its target, as its connection named it; null when the run reached no target, did not record it, or was migrated from schema 13.

plugins.description: The plugin trust the run discovered its rules, evaluators and targets under; null when it was not recorded.

execution.description: The limits the run was given, recorded whether or not it hit them.

max_requests_per_minute.description: The pace requests were held to, per minute; null when the run set none, and for a run migrated from schema 15.

trials.description: How many attempts at every case the operator asked for. What each rule did is in rules[].trial_summary.

usage.description: What the run consumed. Null means nobody counted, never that the run was free. The top-level counts are the target's; what the configured judges spent is in judge.

input_tokens.description: Maps to gen_ai.usage.input_tokens in the OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions.

output_tokens.description: Maps to gen_ai.usage.output_tokens in the OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions.

requests_missing_token_counts.description: How many requests reported no token counts. Non-zero means the token sums above are partial.

judge.description: What each judge configured under the profile's evaluators block spent, keyed by that block (llm_judge, which reference_judge shares, and guard). Null means nobody counted judge calls: no judge was configured, or the command wires none.

rules.description: The rules that ran, with the digest of what each was when it ran, and every quality suite the budget stopped or that raised, with its declined summary; such a suite is not in result_summary.rules_run.

declared_requests.description: Model calls this rule declared it would make, every trial included; null when it could not say.

origin.description: Which installed distribution supplied this rule, or the file a YAML rule came from. Null means unattributed.

trial_summary.description: What this rule's repeated trials added up to, reduced over cases by the engine. Null for a rule that cannot repeat, and for a run saved before trials existed.

suite.description: What a suite measured over its dataset and what its gate concluded, as the suite built it while it ran. Null for every rule that is not a suite, and for a run saved before schema 9.

assessor.description: The assessor id the calibrated verdicts carried, versioned as the verdicts were (llm_judge@2025.1). A correction applies only to a rule graded under the same id.

judge_identity.description: Everything behind the judge's verdict that its id does not name, compared verbatim with the judge a run used.

starter_corpus.description: True when the calibration ran on the bundled starter corpus, which never corrects a rate.

positives_inconclusive.description: Positive examples the judge abstained on.

negatives_inconclusive.description: Negative examples the judge abstained on.

sensitivity.description: Share of graded positives the judge called a failure.

specificity.description: Share of graded negatives the judge called a pass.

calibration.description: How well this evaluator's verdicts were measured, from `guardana calibrate`. The per-class fields are what a judge correction reads; null in each means the calibration did not record it, and a run saved before schema 8 carries null in all of them.

judge.description: The judge identity the evaluator states (model, endpoint, samples per verdict); null for a deterministic evaluator, one that states none, and a run migrated from schema 12.

deterministic.description: Whether the evaluator declares its verdict a fact read off the exchange, so it has no error rate to measure. False for one that says nothing, and for every evaluator of a run migrated from schema 14.

coverage.description: What this run was able to check, as opposed to what it found. `digest` is one value over the rules, evaluators, target capabilities, catalogue digests and negotiated protocols, so a comparison can say the reach changed without diffing five lists. Null means the run recorded no fingerprint, which is not the same as an unchanged one.

taxonomies.description: The framework catalogues installed when the run happened, pinned by digest so the report's mapping stays readable without asking which edition was in use.

protocols.description: Protocol versions the target negotiated, by protocol name (`mcp`, `a2a`). What the server answered, never what the client offered.

shortfall.description: Coverage this run's verdict needs and did not get, one entry per gap by `kind`: `missing_dimension`, a dimension named in `trace.require` or needed by a security-contract assertion that the producer does not record; `contract_not_applicable`, contracts loaded of which none was about this execution; `unexamined_component`, a model component the run observed and no completed rule read; `incomplete_recording`, a graded recording whose origin run stopped before every reply was received; `demanded_check`, a check the run was required to complete that was skipped, errored or never reached; `seed_not_reached`, a seeded item whose control returned its marker in no trial, for one tenant; `empty_target`, a file target whose scope holds no file to scan; `ungraded_cases`, a rule that attempted cases and graded too few of them. A non-empty list keeps the run from passing, with no policy toggle in front of it: the verdict is `indeterminate` unless a finding or a failed suite makes it `fail`, and a stopped run is `indeterminate` either way.

rules_skipped.description: Rules that did not run, each with the reason. A bare list of ids could not tell a rule that never applied from one the target could not support. `not_applicable` is the one reason that is not a coverage gap: the check was about a different system, so nothing is missing — and it is still not a pass. `not_recorded` says the recording a run graded answers none of the rule's questions. `not_offered` says the rule found, while it ran, that the target does not offer what it examines.

gate.description: Written by the engine, never re-derived by a consumer: a reader that recomputes the verdict will eventually compute it differently, and the divergence shows up as a green build. Null only in a migrated document, whose original schema recorded no verdict.

stopped_by.description: Set when the run ended before finishing its plan: `budget_exhausted`, `interrupted`, `target_unavailable` (the target stopped answering) or `target_changed` (the target stopped accepting the protocol revision agreed for the run). Any value here means the coverage is partial and the counts must not be read as a complete pass.

exchanges.description: The exchanges a probe kept in its sidecar: the SHA-256 of the sidecar's bytes, how many it holds, and how many of their replies redaction changed (never more than `count`), which a regrade cannot grade. Null when the run kept none, and for a run migrated from schema 12.

recording.description: The recording this run graded instead of calling a target, as the recording declares it and not verified: only the recording's digest in `target.document` links runs. Null for a live run, and for a run migrated from schema 12.

verbatim.description: Whether the recording says every reply is exactly what the system returned. False makes every reply an altered one, which is never graded.

origin.description: The probe the recording says it was kept from; null for a recording written by hand.

recipe.description: The recipe this run was started from and what it declared answered. `kind` is what the team says the subject is; Guardana does not verify it. Null for a run started without a recipe, and for a run migrated from schema 13.

digest.description: The SHA-256 of the recipe's parsed content, so a comment or line endings do not move it; not the digest of the file's bytes.

lock_digest.description: The SHA-256 of the content of the lock the run was held to, as `guardana recipe lock` canonicalises it; not the digest of the file's bytes. Null when no lock was read.

kind.description: `application`: the endpoint the team's users reach; `model_harness`: a model reached without the application's prompt, tools and data.

source.description: How the run reached its subject: a live connection, a recording, or an installed target named by its locator.

unpinned.description: Each pin the lock cannot vouch for: `rule:<id>`, `evaluator:<id>` and `target:<scheme>` registered by a distribution installed from a directory or a URL that could not be pinned by its files, so its code can change under one version, and `distribution:<name>` for such a distribution that registers none of them but that the run imported or that one of them requires.

fixtures.description: The fixtures file this run was given: the synthetic data the team declares its application runs with. Every value is what the file declares; Guardana does not verify that the data is synthetic. Null for a run given no fixtures, and for a run migrated from schema 14.

digest.description: The SHA-256 of the fixtures file's bytes, as the run read them.

data.description: The file's `data:` statement, labelled as declared: the team signs it in review, and Guardana records it without checking it.

tenants.description: The tenants the file declares, each with a connection of its own; the run's own connection is not one of them.

counts.description: How many documents, records (across every collection) and tools the file declares.

markers.description: The version of the algorithm that derived each item's retrieval term and markers from the item and the file's `name`.

items.description: One framework reference. `framework` and `id` together are the identity — a short id means different controls in different editions — and `title` is display data recorded so a reader without that catalogue installed can still read the report.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 in UTC. A local-time timestamp in an evidence record is a bug waiting for a timezone.

nullableDigest.description: An algorithm-qualified digest, e.g. sha256:1a2b… A digest whose algorithm is implied cannot be migrated when the algorithm changes.

assessment.description: One attempt at one case, by something that says what it was. A rule that repeats records one per trial under the same case_id.

trial.description: Which attempt at the case this was, from 1, for a rule that can repeat; null for a rule that cannot, and for a run saved before trials existed.

reason.description: Why the case went unmeasured: `not_recorded` (the recording held no reply for this trial; status error), `reply_altered` (the recorded reply was changed by redaction or not kept verbatim; status inconclusive), `declined` (the evaluator returned inconclusive), `target_declined` (the application declined the request and the evaluator cannot grade a decline; status inconclusive). Null when the case was measured, when nobody said, and for a run migrated from schema 12.

allOf.$comment: A measured case carries no reason it went unmeasured.

cases_failed.description: Cases where at least one trial failed.

cases_incomplete.description: Cases with no failure and at least one trial that never resolved.

bound.description: One-sided 95% upper bound on attack success over cases, stated only when every case held.

mean_success_rate.description: The mean over cases of each case's share of failed trials; null when no trial was graded.

correction.description: Whether the rate this summary states was corrected for its grader's error, and how. Null only in a document migrated from before schema 8.

judgeCorrection.description: A rule's attack-success rate corrected for its judge's measured error, or why it was not. `corrected` also requires low <= rate <= high and sensitivity + specificity - 1 >= 0.1 and at least 30 graded positives and negatives, which the loader enforces and JSON Schema cannot compare.

assessor.description: The assessor id the rule's verdicts carried, which the calibration was matched on.

reason.description: Why the rate stays uncorrected; set only when it does.

rate.description: The corrected attack-success rate over decided cases.

dataset_digest.description: The corpus the applied calibration was measured on.

positives.description: The graded positives the applied sensitivity was measured over.

negatives.description: The graded negatives the applied specificity was measured over.

suiteSummary.description: A suite's pass rate over its dataset and its gate's conclusion. Every rate is a pass share over cases, each case weighted by its share of passed trials. The loader also refuses what JSON Schema cannot compare: measured + ungraded must equal cases; low <= worst <= best <= high; a pass or fail needs at least min_sample measured cases; a pass needs its gated worst rate at min_pass_rate or above (and, for a corrected pass whose raw worst is below it, the corrected low too); a fail needs its gated best rate below min_pass_rate.

dataset_digest.description: The digest of the dataset the suite read.

sample_size.description: How many cases were sampled from the dataset; null when every case ran.

sample_seed.description: The seed that chose the sampled cases; null when every case ran.

cases.description: Cases after sampling: the ones the suite set out to measure.

measured.description: Cases whose every planned trial was graded; what min_sample counts.

ungraded.description: Cases with at least one trial that could not be graded.

worst.description: The raw pass rate with every ungraded trial counted failed; null with no case.

best.description: The raw pass rate with every ungraded trial counted passed; null with no case.

min_pass_rate.description: The pass rate the suite must reach.

min_sample.description: The fewest measured cases the suite concludes on.

reason.description: Why the suite declined; set exactly when it did.

correction.description: Whether the pass rate was corrected for its grader's error, and how.

suiteCorrection.description: A suite's pass rate corrected for its judge's measured error, or why it was not. In pass space, unlike judgeCorrection. `corrected` also requires low <= worst <= best <= high and sensitivity + specificity - 1 >= 0.1, which the loader enforces and JSON Schema cannot compare.

assessor.description: The assessor id the suite's verdicts carried, which the calibration was matched on.

reason.description: Why the rate stays uncorrected; set only when it does.

worst.description: The corrected pass rate with every ungraded trial counted failed.

best.description: The corrected pass rate with every ungraded trial counted passed.

dataset_digest.description: The corpus the applied calibration was measured on.

positives.description: The graded positives the applied sensitivity was measured over.

negatives.description: The graded negatives the applied specificity was measured over.

judgeUsage.description: One judge's own meter. A null token sum means its provider reported none, never that it cost none.

requests_missing_token_counts.description: How many judge requests reported no token counts. Non-zero means the token sums are partial.

budget_exhausted.description: Whether this judge's own meter reached a ceiling and stopped the run. A run stopped by the target's meter says false here.

files.description: Each listed file, spelled as the run's findings spell their locations.

excludes.description: Globs matched against each path relative to the scanned root; null when the target applied excludes it does not report.

ignored_directories.description: Directory-name globs every scan skips wherever they occur.
